q: Which emits less: laser, plasma or gas cutting of steel?
title: Laser, plasma or gas cutting
short: Laser and plasma run on electricity, so their emissions sit in Scope 2 at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh. Gas cutting burns acetylene or LPG, which is Scope 1, plus bought oxygen in Scope 3. Compare per metre cut at your plate thickness, from meter readings and gas invoices.
audience: Fabrication shops and steel service centres

ul: Laser: electricity for the source and chiller; assist gas such as nitrogen or oxygen.
Plasma: electricity and compressed air or gas.
Gas cutting: acetylene (about 3.38 kg CO2 per kg burned) or LPG (2.98 kg CO2 per kg), plus oxygen.

p: Gas cutting is often used on very thick plate where other methods are slow. Compare on the jobs you actually cut.

ol: Log metres cut per machine for a month.
Read kWh from a sub-meter, and gas from cylinder invoices.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
